title: trqp: QUERY_SLOTS ponytail names wrong ceiling and upgrade
description:
git-vouch-trqp:37-41 (snapshot of 4237c43). The ponytail comment gives the ceiling as "QUERY_SLOTS checks per QUERY_TIMEOUT" and the upgrade as "caching a checked registry (vouch-faq3.6)". Both are off:

1. The binding ceiling is the latency of each request, not concurrency. cmd_query (git-vouch:2499-2516) runs check_registry, which walks the whole first-parent history of people/ with signature checks, on every request. Latency grows with registry history. Once one check takes longer than QUERY_TIMEOUT (30 s, line 36), every request is a retryable 503, however lightly the bridge is loaded. Concurrency is rarely the limit: verify-trust queries one DID at a time (OpenVTC verify-trust crates/verify-trust/src/lib.rs:1175-1220, deduplicated by DID), so the 4-slot cap only bites when 5 or more CI runs overlap.
2. The bridge's decide() ignores resource, but verify-trust re-asks with --fallback-resource after any denial (lib.rs:1197-1215). Every denied DID therefore costs two identical full checks.
3. vouch-faq3.6 tracks periodic sync and staleness reporting. It contains no caching, so the named upgrade path points at nothing.

What goes wrong if left: a maintainer sizing a kernel-scale deployment reads "4 per 30 s" and tunes QUERY_SLOTS. The real limit is check time compared with QUERY_TIMEOUT, and the upgrade has no bead.

Fix (comment first, code optional):
- Restate the ceiling: "one full-history registry check per request; requests fail once a check exceeds QUERY_TIMEOUT". Point the upgrade at a bead that exists, or file one.
- Cheapest upgrade (~10 lines, stdlib): memoize query() answers in a dict keyed by (registry HEAD oid from `git rev-parse HEAD`, entity, at), with a short TTL such as 60 s. The TTL is needed because a key's validity at "now" changes when its retired instant passes, with no commit. One rev-parse costs milliseconds against a full check, and the memo also absorbs the duplicate fallback-resource query.
- Caveat for whoever builds it: query judges the working tree (git-vouch:1100-1101; the test at tests/trqp/test_trqp.py:466 relies on an uncommitted file), so a HEAD key is only sound for a clean served clone. Either state that as a deployment constraint or add `git status --porcelain` to the key.
